resources.string: Phone sensors & Polar H10 → Lab Streaming Layer
This phone reports no streamable sensors.
Applies to continuous sensors; on-change sensors (light, proximity, steps…) stream at an irregular rate.
Microphone permission is required for the audio stream.

Latitude, longitude, altitude, accuracy, speed and bearing, one sample per GPS fix. Most phones deliver at most 1 fix per second, whatever the rate. Works best outdoors; needs precise location permission.
Drag and pinch to move and zoom; Follow centres the map on the latest fix again. Map tiles come from OpenStreetMap over the internet.
Precise location permission is required for the GPS stream.
Phone sensors and audio are stamped with the moment they were measured. Recommended.
Phone sensors and audio are stamped when they reach the app, as SENDA does. Delivery delays of a few to tens of ms end up in the time stamps.
Tap Scan and wear the H10 (wet the electrodes) so it starts advertising.
Select a Polar device first, or switch the Polar H10 off
Bluetooth permissions are required to find and connect to the H10.
Save an XDF file on this phone

Records every stream Sensorium sends, with the same time stamps and meta-data, into one XDF file (as LabRecorder writes). It is saved in Download/Sensorium when streaming stops. LSL streaming continues as usual.
Select at least one sensor, the microphone or a Polar H10
No Wi-Fi / network: LSL consumers on other machines cannot see the streams.
If the recording PC does not see the streams, add this line to the [lab] section of /etc/lsl_api/lsl_api.cfg (Linux/macOS) or lsl_api.cfg next to LabRecorder (Windows), then restart LabRecorder:
Streams the sensors of this phone, its microphone and a Polar H10 chest strap (ECG and accelerometer), and its GPS position, to Lab Streaming Layer.
Sensorium grew out of SENDA by Ali Ayub Khan (NeuropsyOL, University of Oldenburg), rewritten with the Polar H10 support of PolarMobile.
